summary:
The process of extracting an image from FITS is a complex task not only complex but also a time taking process.
LUMEN solves this problem, it requests Right ascension and declination (only in DECIMAL FORM) which uses C++ as its backend.
Although this process is a bit slow, it gives highly detailed images.
details:
As a prototype it hosts a local server from C++ by the httplib, which is also used to get the major required CSV and FITS images.

This code also uses Tinyxml2 which goes through CSV and gets the access_url which is then used to get the FITS images.

The FITS images is converted by a main library in the name CCFits, this might not be a familiar library but it is a C++ mask for CFITSIO a famous library for C which is used to convert FITS images.

Then these pixel images are then converted using OpenCv2
